text:
The Open Door Notes were the 1899 and 1900 diplomatic circulars from U.S. Secretary of State John Hay. They asked the powers with spheres in China to keep trade, harbor dues, and railroad charges equal for every nation, to leave Chinese collection of the treaty tariff in place, and to preserve China’s territorial and administrative integrity. The 1900 note, sent during the Boxer uprising, restated equal and impartial trade and protection of China’s territorial entity as American policy.

CONFIDENCE: 93
